summary: An I2C monitor like the INA219 but with finer steps: 2.5 microvolts on the shunt and 1.25 mV on the bus, plus alert registers and two identification registers.

cite.q: 01h Shunt Voltage Register Shunt voltage measurement data. 00000000 00000000 0000 R
02h Bus Voltage Register Bus voltage measurement data. 00000000 00000000 0000 R

all: being delivered to the load. 00000000 00000000 0000 R
flowing through the shunt resistor. 00000000 00000000 0000 R

cite.q: 06h Mask/Enable Register Alert configuration and Conversion Ready flag. 00000000 00000000 0000 R/ W
FEh Manufacturer ID Register Contains unique manufacturer identification number. 0101010001001001 5449 R
FFh Die ID Register Contains unique die identification number.

facts.text: The shunt voltage register counts in 2.5 microvolt steps.

cite.q: Shunt voltage 2.5 μV Bus voltage 1.25 mV

facts.text: The bus voltage register counts in 1.25 mV steps with no bit shift.
Calibration = 0.00512 / (Current_LSB x Rshunt), truncated to an integer.
The power register's step is fixed at 25 times Current_LSB.

cite.q: internally programmed to equal 25 times the programmed value of the Current_LSB

facts.text: Current register = shunt register x calibration / 2048.
Power register = current register x bus register / 20000.
The datasheet's worked example (20 mV shunt, 12 V bus, 1 mA/bit, 2 mOhm) gives shunt 8000, bus 9584, cal 2560, current 10000 and power 4792. The simulator reproduces all five.
The top bit of the bus voltage register is always zero, since the pin only measures positive voltage.

cite.q: the MSB of the Bus Voltage Register (02h) is always zero

facts.text: Current and power read zero until the Calibration register is programmed.

cite.q: default to '0' because the Calibration register defaults to '0'

notModeled: Conversion times, averaging and operating modes: registers follow the inputs immediately
The reset bit in Configuration, the alert function and the ALERT pin (Mask/Enable and Alert Limit are plain storage)
